solutions.method: Use the ranges of the reciprocal functions and the intersections of the graphs.

steps.explanation: (i) Secant passes through (0,1),(π,−1),(2π,1); add the horizontal line y=3. (ii) There are two intersections, hence two solutions.

(i) Cosecant has vertical asymptotes at −180°,0°,180° and turning points (−90°,−1),(90°,1). The curve −sinx has the opposite sign on each half-interval. (ii) The curves never intersect: the resulting equation sin²x=−1 has no real solution.

solutions.method: Relate each pair by a horizontal shift using the cofunction identities.

steps.explanation: (i) Cotangent has asymptotes at multiples of 180° and zeros at odd multiples of 90°; −tanx has asymptotes at odd multiples of 90° and zeros at multiples of 180°. Both decrease on each branch. (ii) Translate −tanx by 90° horizontally in either direction to obtain cotx.
(i) Secant has asymptotes at odd multiples of π/2; cosecant at multiples of π. Their turning values are ±1. (ii) Translate secx by π/2 to the right to obtain cosecx.

solutions.solutionHtml:

  2. (i) Secant has asymptotes at odd multiples of π/2; cosecant at multiples of π. Their turning values are ±1. (ii) Translate secx by π/2 to the right to obtain cosecx.
